| `reserved` negative | `release` never refused a committed order, and `expire` released any old order whatever its status. So the nightly job subtracted units that had already moved to `sold`. Concurrent releases subtracted twice. |
| Held twice on retry | `reserve` checked for an existing order before the first attempt had saved one, so an overlapping retry held the stock again. |
| Bundle item stayed held | `reserve` saved each item's hold as it went. When a later item was short (or unknown), the earlier holds stayed, and there was no order record to release them from. |
| `sold` above orders shipped | Concurrent commits both passed the status check. A commit racing a release or `expire` applied both. `expire` also flipped committed orders to `released` while leaving `sold` counted. |

## Fix

- **`src/keyed-lock.js` (new):** a lock per key. Calls that share a key run one at a time, in arrival order. Calls with nothing in common don't wait for each other, so this avoids the service-wide lock rolled back after INC-5490. Keys are always taken in sorted order, which stops two bundles that list the same SKUs in different orders from deadlocking. Keys are forgotten once nobody is using them, so memory doesn't grow with every SKU and order ever seen.
- **`src/inventory.js`:**
  - Order changes take the order's lock first, then the lock for each SKU. The public API and error types are unchanged.
  - `reserve` checks for an existing order while holding the order's lock, and checks every item before saving anything.
  - `release` now rejects committed orders with `OrderStateError`.
  - `expire` re-reads each order under its lock and releases only orders still in `reserved`.
  - If a store write fails partway through, the writes already made are undone and the error is re-thrown. If the undo also fails, both errors are reported together in an `AggregateError`.

## Tests

- **`tests/inc-5521.test.js`:** one group per symptom, plus a randomized stress test that mixes reserves, retries, commits, releases and `expire` against a store with random delays. The stress test checks that every counter matches the orders in the store. All 17 symptom tests failed on the old code.
- **`tests/keyed-lock.test.js`:** unit tests for the lock.
- **Checking the tests:** in a scratch copy I broke five things one at a time: no key sorting, no key cleanup, no undo, locks per service instance instead of per store, and a service-wide lock. At least one test failed each time. The service-wide lock failed only the "calls that share nothing don't wait" test. The stress test also passed under 20 other random seeds.

## Assumptions and limits

- **Workers share one process.** The locks only coordinate calls within one process. That matches staging, where an in-process lock stopped the overselling. Workers in separate processes would need atomic operations in the store itself, and `get`/`set`/`keys` can't provide that.
- **Locks follow the store.** Two service objects built on the same store share locks, so running several services in one process is also safe.
- **Undoing failed writes goes slightly beyond the report.** A failed store write could otherwise leave the same stuck hold the incident describes, so I included it.
- **A hung store call blocks its keys.** It holds those locks until it returns. I didn't add timeouts, because releasing a lock while a write might still land would bring the race back.

**Process notes:**
- `dx run-gate` isn't installed here, so I ran `npm test` directly.
- There is no git remote, so the commit is local only. A repo hook required a conventional commit subject and the Dex co-author line, so I amended the commit to match.
- I didn't add a README because this is a bug fix in an existing project.

**Possible follow-up (not built):** repair the SKUs whose `reserved` is already negative in production. That needs a one-off job that recomputes the counters from the order records.
